test_title: PYST 2: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: maths
question: The ratio of the distance between two places A and B to the distance between places B and C is 3 ∶ 5. A man travels from A to B at a speed of x km/h and from B to C at a speed of 50 km/h. If his average speed for the entire journey is 40 km/h, then what is the value of (x – 10) : ( x + 1)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the distances AB and BC be 3 units and 5 units respectively.

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

40 = (3 + 5) ÷ (3/x + 5/50)

40 = 8 ÷ (3/x + 1/10) ⇒ 1/5 = 3/x + 1/10

3/x = 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 ⇒ x = 30 km/h.

Ratio = (30 − 10) : (30 + 1) = 20 : 31.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance Ratio AB : BC = 3 : 5

Speed A to B = x km/h, Speed B to C = 50 km/h

Average Speed = 40 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/416c85945ccaeaef5402951885accf1b8fd8386be24f4e79740ef34a8f26031d.png] 

Formula: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

⇒ Total Distance = 3d + 5d = 8d

⇒ Time (AB) = 3d / x

⇒ Time (BC) = 5d / 50 = d / 10

⇒ 40 = 8d ÷ (3d/x + d/10)

⇒ 40 = 8 ÷ (3/x + 1/10)

⇒ 3/x + 1/10 = 8 / 40

⇒ 3/x + 1/10 = 1/5

⇒ 3/x = 1/5 − 1/10

⇒ 3/x = 1/10

⇒ x = 30

Now, evaluate (x − 10) : (x + 1):

⇒ (30 − 10) : (30 + 1)

⇒ 20 : 31

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Weighted Average Speed

For different distances d₁, d₂,... and speeds v₁, v₂,..., Average Speed = (Σdᵢ) ÷ (Σdᵢ/vᵢ).

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).</p
